header.title: KV 9: Grab Ramses' VI.〈, Korridor C, Nische am Ende der linken Wand〉: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Literary texts
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:sawlit:kv-9-grab-ramses-vi-korridor-c-nische-am-ende-der-linken-wan:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.1.1: Much of this text is restored by the editor; all bracketed words are restorations. The king is Ramesses VI. Line 1: ꜥft,t is uncertain, perhaps a shrine or chest. mn ('N', the placeholder for the speaker's name) stands beside the king's name in lines 13, 15 and 17; in line 13 it may be the name of a being. Line 13: {k} is deleted by the editor. Line 21: skk rnp,t, 'brings the years to an end', may mean 'passes the years'; {k}[nb] nṯr=f, '[lord] of his god', is obscure. Line 22: the restored sꜥḥ may be 'rank' or 'raising'; rd[.pl] [štꜣ,w] is literally 'feet [secret]'. Line 28: ꜥꜣ may be 'door' or 'great one'.

nodes.text: Spell [for] [this] [*ꜥft.t*(?)].
[Nun] [was embraced] by the Great One himself.
He says to the gods who come forth [in] [the east] [of] [the sky]:
[Give] [praise] to the great god from whom I came into being.

It is I who made the sky and [established] [it], to place the bas of the gods in it, I being with them forever, the Osiris King, Lord of the Two Lands Nebmaatre-meriamun, Son of Ra Ramesses-Amenherkhepeshef-netjer-heqaiunu, [justified], with them forever, who gives birth to the years.
My ba is magic.
He is greater than it.
The ba of Shu is the wind.
The ba of Heh is the rain.
The ba of Darkness is the night.
The ba of Nun is the water.
The ba of Osiris is the Ram of Mendes.
The ba of [Sobek] is the croco[dile]; [and] the ba of every god and every goddess is in the snakes; and the ba of N is in [Bakhu]; and the ba of Ra is in magic [throughout] [the whole] [land].
[Spoken] by a man when he makes his protection [with] magic:
The King, [Lord of the Two Lands] [Nebmaatre-meriamun], [Son of Ra] [Ramesses-Amenherkhepeshef]-netjer-heqaiunu, N, is that [pure] magic which is in the mouth and the body of Ra.
Gods, [akh-spirits] and [dead], [be far] [from] him!
Son of Ra, lord of appearances, Rames[ses-Amenherkhepeshef-netjer-heqaiunu], N, is Ra, the akh.
Then you shall say: [you] pass by in the evening and at dawn.
[Down] on your face, enemy of Ra!
King of Upper and Lower Egypt, Lord of the Two Lands Nebmaatre-meriamun, the pure ba of magic.

O lord of eternity, who created everlastingness, who brings the years to an end(?), [in whom] the gods go down and come forth every day, [lord] of his god, ruler who made himself, beloved of his fathers the gods,

to whom Thoth gives praise [and] [rank] [of] [the sky] [upon] [him], to whom Shu gives his arm, [saying]: 'I have been rescued [from] [these] [two] [great] [gods] [...] great ones, [who sit] [in] [the east] [of] [the sky], [guardians] [of] [the sky], [who guard] [the earth], [hidden] of feet.'
[Then] [they] [say]:
[How great] he is when he goes forth [to] [see] [Nun]!
Then they say:
[He is] a god [in] [truth].
[Then] [they] [say]:
[He] [has] [reached] [the] [door] on [the] [road].
[I] [know] [the ba] [of] [this] [god] [whose] [face] [is] [that of] [Herishef].
